sentences.en: I've been really trying to prioritize my health in a realistic way this year, and something that has kept me really motivated is my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 今年我一直在努力以一种现实的方式优先考虑自己的健康，而让我保持动力的东西就是我的 WHOOP。

sentences.en: I am such a data person, which is why I love WHOOP, because I can genuinely see why my body feels differently depending on the day, why I'm running differently,
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常看重数据的人，这就是我喜欢 WHOOP 的原因，因为我可以清楚地看到为什么我的身体在不同日子里会有不同的感觉，为什么我的跑步状态会有所不同，

sentences.en: why I'm maybe less focused.
sentences.zh: 为什么我有时会注意力不集中。

sentences.en: WHOOP effortlessly tracks my sleep, it tracks my strain, my recovery, my stress, and most importantly, my overall health.
sentences.zh: WHOOP 可以轻松追踪我的睡眠、压力、恢复情况、紧张程度，最重要的是，我的整体健康状况。

sentences.en: And it just gives me all that data and all those patterns so I can make better decisions, which includes knowing when to go easy and knowing when to go hard.
sentences.zh: 它为我提供了所有这些数据和模式，让我能够做出更好的决策，包括知道什么时候该放松，什么时候该努力。

sentences.en: New members can try WHOOP with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新用户可以在订阅会员之前，先通过 30 天免费试用体验 WHOOP。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 请访问 join.whoop.com/psychology，即可免费获得一个月的 WHOOP 会员资格。

sentences.zh: 有些人会保留他们所有的旧演出门票。

sentences.en: It brings back the music, it brings back the memories, even the smells.
sentences.zh: 它能带回音乐，带回记忆，甚至带回当时的气味。

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 还有人收集香水瓶、咖啡杯、外国纸币，或是 80 年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是非常私人的事情。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它不仅诉说着我们是谁，也诉说着我们从哪里来。

sentences.zh: 在新的播客节目《Charmed with Sam Todd》中，

sentences.en: Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: Sam 探索了那些成为我们生命一部分的记忆、执念和微小的珍宝。

sentences.en: Charmed with Sam Todd.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《Charmed with Sam Todd》。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《20 多岁的心理学》，这是一档探讨我们在 20 多岁时经历的一些重大人生变化和转折的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们的心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, dive into the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要深入探讨 20 多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: How are you going?
sentences.zh: 你们最近怎么样？

sentences.en: How have we all been?
sentences.zh: 大家都好吗？

sentences.en: It's been a while since I asked that, and I'm not expecting an answer since this is kind of just me in this room right now recording.
sentences.zh: 我已经很久没问过这个问题了，而且我并不指望能得到回答，因为现在房间里只有我一个人在录音。

sentences.en: But sometimes it feels nice to just imagine you all on the other side, listening in your car or at work or at the gym whilst you're cleaning the house.
sentences.zh: 但有时想象你们都在另一端，在车里、在工作中、在健身房或者在打扫房间时收听，感觉真的很不错。

sentences.en: I hope you're all doing amazing and there is something great you are looking forward to or something you're especially grateful in life at the moment.
sentences.zh: 希望你们都过得很好，并且生活中有什么让你们期待的，或者有什么让你们此刻感到特别感恩的事情。

sentences.en: This week's topic is a little bit heavy and might be rather intense for some people, perhaps very vulnerable and revealing.
sentences.zh: 本周的话题有点沉重，对某些人来说可能相当强烈，甚至可能非常脆弱和坦白。

sentences.en: So I thought it would be nice to just start out with something positive to focus on before we jump straight in because today we are going to be talking about father wounds
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在深入探讨之前，先从一些积极的事情开始会比较好，因为今天我们要讨论的是“父亲创伤”，

sentences.en: and the ways in which our relationship with our father within the family dynamic can lead to a lot of difficult beliefs, difficult emotions, difficult behaviours later in life.
sentences.zh: 以及我们在家庭动态中与父亲的关系如何导致后来生活中许多困难的信念、情绪和行为。

sentences.en: Father wounds are really complex and really difficult and they emerge from a myriad of different experiences, mainly our fathers being absent in our childhood,
sentences.zh: 父亲创伤非常复杂且难以处理，它们源于无数不同的经历，主要是父亲在我们的童年时期缺席，

sentences.en: being emotionally or physically unavailable, consistently prioritising work over family, not taking on a positive and active role in our lives, perhaps being abusive.
sentences.zh: 在情感或身体上无法陪伴，总是把工作置于家庭之上，没有在我们的生活中承担积极主动的角色，甚至可能存在虐待行为。

sentences.en: Anything that disrupted the dynamic or relationship between you, the child, and your father, the caregiver, can result in this form of unresolved trauma or disconnect.
sentences.zh: 任何破坏了你（孩子）与父亲（照顾者）之间动态或关系的事情，都可能导致这种形式的未解决创伤或疏离感。

sentences.en: Divorce, cheating, alcoholism, a few other examples, remarriage, having a new younger family, these are all things that disturb or injure
sentences.zh: 离婚、出轨、酗酒，还有其他一些例子，比如再婚、有了新的年幼家庭，这些都是会扰乱或伤害

sentences.en: the connection and the attachment that we have with this important figure in our lives and it can be really formative and impactful.
sentences.zh: 我们与生命中这个重要人物之间的联系和依恋的事情，这可能会产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: People sometimes call it daddy issues.
sentences.zh: 人们有时称之为“恋父情结”（daddy issues）。

sentences.en: I don't love that term, especially in a clinical sense because it's become very poppy, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢这个词，特别是在临床意义上，因为它变得太流行了，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And I also think that it has been reduced to kind of shame women in particular for their sexuality.
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为它被简化了，用来羞辱女性，特别是针对她们的性行为。

sentences.en: You know, she likes to have a lot of sex because she has daddy issues.
sentences.zh: 比如，“她喜欢频繁发生性关系是因为她有恋父情结”。

sentences.en: It's a lot more complex than that.
sentences.zh: 这比那复杂得多。

sentences.en: And I think this kind of language is quite reductive.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种语言相当具有还原论色彩。

sentences.en: As with anything that has to do with psychology and our mental health and our emotional state and our behaviours, the explanation is not always as simple
sentences.zh: 正如任何与心理学、心理健康、情绪状态和行为相关的事情一样，解释并不总是像我们

sentences.en: or simplistic as we might hear on social media or as might be displayed online.
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体上听到的或网上展示的那样简单或简化。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time, our father wounds really only begin to be revealed as we grow older, especially in our early or late 20s, sometimes even later for some people
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们的父亲创伤只有在我们长大后才开始显露，尤其是在 20 多岁初期或后期，对有些人来说甚至更晚，

sentences.en: when we have left the orbit of our family, we have flown the nest, we are beginning to see what may have been normal for other people that was not the case for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 当我们离开了家庭的轨道，离开了家，我们开始看到对别人来说可能很正常的事情，对我们自己却并非如此。

sentences.en: I think we are given both the gift and the curse of hindsight and the ability to compare our childhood history with our friends' experiences.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们既拥有事后诸葛亮的礼物，也背负着它的诅咒，我们有能力将自己的童年历史与朋友的经历进行比较。

sentences.en: And when we do that, often, if you are someone who has a father wound, a gap emerges.
sentences.zh: 当我们这样做时，如果你是一个有父亲创伤的人，往往会出现一道鸿沟。

sentences.en: You begin to see that you might not just be an angry person or a sad person or a reactive person or someone who lacks confidence and trust in themselves.
sentences.zh: 你开始意识到，你可能不仅仅是一个爱生气、悲伤、反应过度，或者缺乏自信和自我信任的人。

sentences.en: It's actually a lot deeper than that.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这要深刻得多。

sentences.en: And the truth is contained in our childhood memories.
sentences.zh: 真相就蕴含在我们的童年记忆中。

sentences.en: It's not all about your personality.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全关乎你的个性。

sentences.en: You were not destined to be this individual.
sentences.zh: 你并非注定要成为这样的人。

sentences.en: There was something that emerged between you and your caregiver that has created a whole pattern, a whole flow-on effect of things that as an adult,
sentences.zh: 在你和你的照顾者之间出现了一些事情，创造了一整套模式，一连串的连锁反应，以至于作为成年人，

sentences.en: you're only now just working through.
sentences.zh: 你现在才刚刚开始处理这些问题。

sentences.en: I think as we grow into our adult selves, we often become a lot more reflective and critical of our childhood experiences.
sentences.zh: 我认为随着我们成长为成年人，我们往往会对童年经历进行更多的反思和批判。

sentences.en: We think back on the things that we had to accept or at least tolerate as children when we were dependent on our caregivers, when we were powerless and vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 我们回想起作为孩子时不得不接受或至少忍受的事情，那时我们依赖于照顾者，那时我们无力且脆弱。

sentences.en: And now, as independent people, we can be a bit more honest about it because we don't need to be kind of in a survival mode.
sentences.zh: 而现在，作为独立的人，我们可以更诚实地面对它，因为我们不需要处于那种生存模式中。

sentences.en: That honesty often reveals things that we have suppressed or avoided thinking about for a long time out of a need for self-preservation.
sentences.zh: 这种诚实往往会揭示出我们出于自我保护的需要，长期以来一直压抑或避免去想的事情。

sentences.en: We didn't know what we know now.
sentences.zh: 我们当时并不知道现在所知道的一切。

sentences.en: We were just kids who accepted the standard that was set for us.
sentences.zh: 我们只是接受了为我们设定的标准的孩子。

sentences.en: And we didn't yet have the cognitive or the mental skills to kind of rationalize our experiences and have an adult understanding of what occurred, or we felt was pain.
sentences.zh: 我们当时还没有认知或心理技能来合理化我们的经历，并以成人的理解力去理解所发生的事情，或者我们所感受到的痛苦。

sentences.en: And this can be a really scary thing to unpack because we don't like to see our parents, our fathers as being fallible or even human for so long.
sentences.zh: 解开这些心结可能会非常可怕，因为我们长期以来都不愿看到父母、父亲是会犯错的，甚至是普通人。

sentences.en: They have this almost godlike status in our minds.
sentences.zh: 他们在我们心中有着近乎神一般的地位。

sentences.en: They can do anything, say anything.
sentences.zh: 他们可以做任何事，说任何话。

sentences.en: They are everything.
sentences.zh: 他们就是一切。

sentences.en: So it feels strange to think that this person who we entrusted with all of our needs may have done something to harm us either knowingly or unknowingly.
sentences.zh: 所以，想到这个我们托付了所有需求的人，可能在有意或无意中伤害了我们，感觉很奇怪。

sentences.en: Unconsciously as well, we may not even realize that this is what has happened and that there are certain dysfunctional habits or patterns in our romantic relationships
sentences.zh: 同样在潜意识里，我们可能甚至没有意识到这就是发生的事情，并且在我们的浪漫关系、

sentences.en: and our professional careers and our friendships
sentences.zh: 职业生涯和友谊中存在某些功能失调的习惯或模式，

sentences.en: that all come back to our childhood.
sentences.zh: 这些都追溯到我们的童年。

sentences.en: There is a lot of resentment perhaps that comes up later in life when your parents do get older and you suddenly realize that you have to take care of them
sentences.zh: 当父母变老，你突然意识到你必须照顾他们时，生活中可能会出现很多怨恨，

sentences.en: and there are certain things that you haven't quite worked through or maybe you are about to become a parent, you are considering having children and you're like,
sentences.zh: 而有些事情你还没有完全处理好，或者你即将成为父母，你正在考虑要孩子，你会想：

sentences.en: I don't want to repeat what I experienced.
sentences.zh: 我不希望重蹈覆辙。

sentences.en: There's a sense of inadequacy because there was never a good example set for you.
sentences.zh: 因为从来没有人为你树立过好的榜样，所以会有一种无能感。

sentences.en: There is so much to be said about the impact that these wounds have and there is a lot of misinformation.
sentences.zh: 关于这些创伤的影响，有很多话要说，而且存在很多误导信息。

sentences.en: They have become, this idea, this concept of father wounds has become somewhat of a buzzword and with that we often become detached from what is really occurring
sentences.zh: 它们已经变成了一个流行词，随之而来的是，我们往往与我们在心理和情感层面上，

sentences.en: in our unconscious, subconscious minds on a very psychological and emotional level.
sentences.zh: 在潜意识中真正发生的事情脱节了。

sentences.en: We aren't exactly clear on what it means to have a father wound from an attachment perspective and we aren't exactly clear on where to go from there.
sentences.zh: 我们并不完全清楚从依恋的角度来看，拥有父亲创伤意味着什么，也不完全清楚从哪里开始解决。

sentences.en: How do we work through this on our own, maybe with our family, with a romantic partner?
sentences.zh: 我们如何独自处理这个问题，或者与家人、伴侣一起处理？

sentences.en: Is forgiveness the best policy?
sentences.zh: 原谅是最好的策略吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: I think it requires more than that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这需要更多的努力。

sentences.en: There is an acknowledgement of our father wounds that at some point we're all going to have to do, we're all going to have to reflect on and I want to talk about it today
sentences.zh: 我们需要承认父亲创伤，在某个时刻我们都必须这样做，我们都必须反思，我想今天谈谈这个话题，

sentences.en: starting of course with a theoretical premises for why these occur.
sentences.zh: 当然要从这些创伤发生的理论前提开始。

sentences.en: So a lot of the research that father wounds are based around comes back to attachment theory, one of the most well-known, I think, concepts and doctrines in psychology.
sentences.zh: 关于父亲创伤的大部分研究都回归到依恋理论，我认为这是心理学中最著名的概念和学说之一。

sentences.en: I'm sure we've all heard of it before but for a brief refresher, attachment theory was first introduced by two psychologists,
sentences.zh: 我相信我们都听说过，但简单回顾一下，依恋理论最初是由两位心理学家提出的，

sentences.en: John Bowlby and Mary Ainsworth and it followed their observations of children,
sentences.zh: 约翰·鲍尔比（John Bowlby）和玛丽·安斯沃思（Mary Ainsworth），它源于他们对儿童的观察，

sentences.en: specifically like quite young children, infants almost and they exposed these infants to the situations in which their parents were absent or they were approached by a stranger
sentences.zh: 特别是相当年幼的儿童，几乎是婴儿，他们将这些婴儿置于父母缺席、陌生人接近、

sentences.en: or they were left in a strange situation and they observed their interactions and from that they came to this conclusion that the child's relationship with their caregiver
sentences.zh: 或被留在陌生环境中的情境中，并观察他们的互动。由此他们得出结论：孩子与照顾者的关系

sentences.en: would predict how they behaved in this strange situation and from their behaviors we could categorize these children into attachment styles.
sentences.zh: 可以预测他们在这种陌生环境中的行为，根据这些行为，我们可以将这些孩子归类为不同的依恋类型。

sentences.en: As children, we have some very core physical, emotional,
sentences.zh: 作为孩子，我们有一些非常核心的身体、情感、

sentences.en: mental, even social needs and we are entirely reliant on our parents to fulfill these for us.
sentences.zh: 心理，甚至社交需求，我们完全依赖父母来满足这些需求。

sentences.en: This, of course, includes the need for security, the need for emotional safety and availability, for comfort, for food, for love.
sentences.zh: 这当然包括对安全感、情感上的安全和陪伴、安慰、食物、爱的需求。

sentences.en: Not every parent meets their children's needs in the same way or in the way that their child requires.
sentences.zh: 并非每个父母都能以同样的方式或孩子所需要的方式满足他们的需求。

sentences.en: It is just a sad fact of life.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人悲伤的生活事实。

sentences.en: Some people do not know how to be parents.
sentences.zh: 有些人不知道如何做父母。

sentences.en: They do not know how to provide for their children and this is often very generational.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道如何供养孩子，这通常是非常代际的。

sentences.en: Our parents, our fathers, behave the way that they did and that they do because of how their parents acted who were the way that they were because of their upbringing
sentences.zh: 我们的父母、我们的父亲之所以那样做，是因为他们的父母就是那样做的，而他们的父母之所以那样，是因为他们的成长环境，

sentences.en: and that can get passed down to us through parenting styles and the cycle continues through the impact on our behaviours or when we perhaps want to or do have our own children.
sentences.zh: 这可以通过教养方式传给我们，这种循环通过对我们行为的影响，或者当我们想要或确实有了自己的孩子时，继续下去。

sentences.en: The only model that we have for a parent-child relationship is dysfunctional.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的唯一亲子关系模型是功能失调的。

sentences.en: How our needs were met or not met in childhood affects how we relate to ourselves and others in relationships, in parenting, in friendships when it comes to our self-esteem,
sentences.zh: 我们在童年时期需求是否得到满足，影响着我们在关系、育儿、友谊中如何对待自己和他人，以及我们的自尊、

sentences.en: our independence, our ability to deal with conflict and so much more.
sentences.zh: 独立性、处理冲突的能力等等。

sentences.en: Now, according to attachment theory, people who grew up with supportive and present caregivers are more likely to develop a secure attachment style.
sentences.zh: 根据依恋理论，在支持性和在场的照顾者身边长大的孩子，更有可能形成安全型依恋。

sentences.en: That's about 65% of us according to recent estimates.
sentences.zh: 根据最近的估计，这大约占我们总数的 65%。

sentences.en: By contrast, those with less engaged caregivers, possibly people who have a father wound,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，那些照顾者参与度较低的人，可能就是有父亲创伤的人，

sentences.en: we are more likely to develop an insecure attachment style such as an avoidant or an anxious attachment style.
sentences.zh: 我们更有可能形成不安全型依恋，例如回避型或焦虑型依恋。

sentences.en: A father wound can contribute to these forms of insecure attachment and it is what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 父亲创伤会导致这些形式的不安全依恋，正如其名。

sentences.en: It is an emotional mark, a scar, a psychological scar, left from an experience that maybe caused us pain, some emotional discomfort and distress even if we didn't realize
sentences.zh: 它是一种情感印记，一道伤疤，一道心理创伤，留自于某种可能导致我们痛苦、情感不适和困扰的经历，即使我们直到很久以后才意识到。

sentences.en: it until much later on.
sentences.zh: 某种伤害已经造成了，所以当你走向世界，想要与非照顾者的人建立依恋关系时，你唯一的基础就是

sentences.en: Some kind of damage was done and so when you go out into the world and want to form attachments with people who are not your caregivers, the only basis you have for
sentences.zh: 你与父母之间的依恋关系。

sentences.en: what that should look like is the attachment you have with your parents.
sentences.zh: 他们是我们关系的榜样，当我们谈论父亲创伤时，他们就是我们与男性关系的榜样。
